steps.content: The interrogation room's lights hang dim and cold, cutting through the space like a dull blade and carving it into stark halves of shadow and glare. You and Xiaofeng sit across from each other, separated by mere inches of table, though it might as well be worlds.
The standoff stretches. Finally, a grin breaks across her face, wide and toothy, but her eyes remain cold.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: What happened? You were all chatty before. Something got your tongue?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Well? Spit it out. What's this all about?
The smile curves on her lips, but it never touches her eyes.
This is MBCC. DisCity's agency for handling Sinners.
Look, I know you're pissed. I get it. Let's just... take a breath. Talk this through.
Xiaofeng tilts her head slightly, and a laugh escapes her lips.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Course you get it. Big Noms Chief's got rules to follow. Can't be seen running around with some stray, right?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Go on, then. Let's hear it. Sooner you talk, sooner I'm out of this box.
Xiaofeng leans back, slouching against the chair with an air of ease until you notice those slit pupils locking onto you, unblinking. A chill runs down your spine.
...I'm sorry. I didn't want this. But there's a way things have to be done.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You lay the file on the table between you. It contains a detailed record of the damage Xiaofeng has inflicted across Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: The hell's that? Can't read your fancy papers.
...It's a compiled record of the damage you've caused throughout Syndicate since entering DisCity.

A meat stall robbed, a jewelry store hit, and kids snatched from the park... Setting aside the potential ramifications of smuggling and illegal entry, your actions have directly damaged the property and safety of West District residents. I had no choice but to step in.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Heh. Funny. I remember helping you bag those smugglers. Didn't see any medal for that.
You did... And the way you did it left the streets looking like a warzone. Catching bad guys doesn't erase the cleanup.
I'm sorry. But my job—my first job—as the MBCC Chief is keeping citizens safe.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tch. All these damn rules, twisting everything around. Good's good. Bad's bad. Why make it messy?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Ha. Should've known. Here I was thinking we were the same kind. Thought maybe we could run together. Eat, drink, stir up some fun... Guess I was the fool. Some smiles don't mean a thing.
You know exactly what Xiaofeng wants to hear: if you toss these files aside right now and ask her to continue your adventures together, she agrees in a heartbeat.
But you have your own principles to uphold.

We can't allow an S-Class Sinner to roam DisCity unchecked. But fortunately, regulations on Sinners aren't as strict as they used to be. We've had cases of foreign Sinners being granted parole before.
I promise, as long as you cooperate and pass the evaluations, I'll fight to secure you as much freedom as possible.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...Freedom?
Xiaofeng leans back in her chair. There is a slight softening in her tone now.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Fine. What kind of freedom?

Within the Bureau, many Sinners continue to pursue personal interests and maintain individual lifestyles. We do not impose blanket restrictions on daily conduct. You can continue living as you normally would.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Mm... Figured. So you're slapping one of those shackle things on me?

Correct. I require the ability to monitor your location and, if necessary, to enforce compliance. However, as long as your behavior remains within acceptable parameters, I will not interfere with your activities.
Because... I know that you don't act out of malice.
You look at Xiaofeng. By now, you understand her nature. She is not so much a person as a wild thing descended from the deep mountains.

Strength grants her simplicity. Her mind works in straight lines, untouched by the weight of others' opinions. When someone catches her interest, she plays with them for sport. The moment that interest fades, she vanishes, never lingering.
Many of the Sinners here are similar to you, restless, with more energy than constructive outlets. That's where friction comes from.
With the right channels—assignments, missions, objectives—those tensions can be redirected. I'll ensure you have access to those opportunities.
And if your evaluations come back favorable, you could earn expanded privileges. More time outside the facility—
You don't get to finish. At the keyword, Xiaofeng lunges forward like a predator seizing prey, closing the distance in an instant and cutting you off.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: How long outside? What do I have to do? And how much can I push it?
...It depends on the individual case. But I'll secure whatever latitude I can.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...There it is. You can't even give me a straight answer.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: I've seen that type. Soon as they get a little authority, all they care about is covering their own hide. If I'm so dangerous, someone who needs locking up right now, then your bosses wouldn't let me roam free for a second.

Before she finishes speaking, she lunges, the motion too fast for you to do anything but flinch. Her hand sweeps toward the folder at your side, fingertips hooking the pages inside, and with one sharp jerk, she tears them free.

They scatter through the air like snow: approval numbers, red stamps, classified text—all of it flashes once under the light and dissolves into chaos. Amid the swirling mess, Xiaofeng's eyes find their target with predatory precision. Her hand darts out and seizes a single page.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Can't read much. But I know my own name when I see it.
She glances down at the paper and then back up at you, her smile cold and never reaching her eyes.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Go on, then, Tiny. Read it to me. What's it say?
Slap. The paper hits the table squarely in front of you. The enlarged, bolded Eastian characters stare up, stark and unforgiving.
Silence stretches between you, and Xiaofeng's gaze cuts through it, sharp as a blade, piercing every careful word you have laid down.
Those words mean nothing now. You have no choice. You must tell her the truth.
...I've been ordered to detain you. And to process your deportation back to Eastia. There's a deadline.
You gather the scattered documents, and beyond the dense text of your action reports, you find another file: an investigation report.
I know an Eastian scholar who specializes in mythology. After hearing about the White Tiger Mountain Lord, I reached out. She came back with some interesting findings.

In Eastia, there's a mountain range called White Tiger. Stretches hundreds of miles. Local legend says a tiger deity lives there. Offer tribute, and the deity grants safe passage through the mountains.

The myth paints a peaceful picture, but reality's messier. Wildlife and humans still clash, hunting each other, fighting over territory. But there are accounts of something unusual. Some claim they've seen a human figure... walking alongside a white tiger.
Whether there's truly a deity on White Tiger Mountain isn't something we can verify. But we can confirm one thing with reasonable certainty. A powerful human lives there.
Someone strong enough to command a white tiger. Someone who earned the title "Mountain Lord." In DisCity terms, an S-Class Sinner.
You lift your gaze and lock eyes with Xiaofeng.
Xiaofeng. That person is you.

I understand now. The smuggling, the fights, and even what happened at Northsnow Manor... You were just bored. You weren't trying to cause harm. You were simply playing, passing the time, and having fun. To you, chaos is just... entertainment.
But to ordinary people, what you call entertainment is a <color=#fb9259>disaster</color>.

That's why DisCity doesn't want an unpredictable variable like you roaming freely within its borders. And I... I'm genuinely glad you came to see me. But perhaps we can find a better way forward. Something more stable and safer, for both of us.
The room falls silent. Xiaofeng isn't smiling. For the first time, her gaze shifts away, and something uneasy stirs in your chest.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...Heh. So that's how you see me...

Clang! The woman across from you explodes into motion. Her restraints shriek warnings and then snap apart as a blur streaks across the table's edge. You barely raise your hand before a tremendous force slams you back into your chair.

Metal screeches as the shackles on her hands twist and break completely. She slips past your defenses with ease and slams you against the wall, one hand pinning you there. Her cold fingertips find your throat.
Ugh!
Xiaofeng bares her teeth in a grin, stark white fangs flashing, and a low laugh escapes her throat.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Too strong, so I'm dangerous? Might hurt someone, so I should roll over and let you put a leash on me?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tiny... do you even know what a "Mountain Lord" really is?
Her cold fingertips trail slowly along your neck, hovering and teasing, until they find your pulse. They begin to tighten. And when she speaks, her voice drips with danger.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: You humans... Soon as you leave the mountains behind, soon as your bellies are full, you love looking down on everything else. Passing judgment. Forgetting what it took to survive out there.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Being a <color=#fb9259>Mountain Lord</color>... First, you live through the endless snowstorms. Then you sink your fangs into every beast that challenges you. Fight for every scrap of food. Every inch of ground. No one speaks pretty out there. You lose once, and you're dead.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: You fight until nothing dares challenge you anymore. Then you're safe, for a while. But you're always watching, waiting for the next cub that grows strong enough to kill you and take your place... That's the mountain. It's either they die, or you die.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Heh... Funny, isn't it? Humans don't raise their young but dump them in the mountains. Leave them for the tigers to drag off. If it weren't for this "Mania" you keep talking about, I would've frozen solid in the first storm.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tell me, if there really was some great deity on White Tiger Mountain... why didn't they come for me first?
You...

Overlooked details click into place, forming a single clear conclusion: Xiaofeng disregards rules because she was never taught them, never civilized, never truly human. She survives on forest and instinct alone.
She lowers her head now, leaning close to your neck. Her breath falls warm across your skin. It takes you a moment to understand... that she is smelling you.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Heh, relax. I don't care about any of that. It's just... some fools can't tell the difference. They mistake me for some tiger deity, come begging for blessings. But the second they see real teeth, they piss themselves and run...

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Isn't that rich? This is exactly what they asked for. They're just lying to themselves.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Humans never raised me. By rights, I don't owe your rules a damn thing. But you...

The pressure on your throat increases, and Mania flows from the point where her hand meets your skin. The shackles surge within you, lunging toward the "enemy" before you. You fight to hold them back, but Xiaofeng only grows more excited by your struggle.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Hahahaha! There it is!

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: I can smell it. You're just like me... But you've been caged too long. By this little iron box. By that buzzing little communicator. By all those obedient, foolish Sinners wagging their tails for you...

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: And by whatever ideas they poured into your head! Who knows where they came from!

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: "Greater good." "Justice." "Heroism." Just pretty words. That girl with the plum stick, she's the same. You could both be free like me...
Her hand tightens further around your throat, your vision blurs, and the violent pounding of your heart thunders in your ears.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Why not just live free and easy?
Xiaofeng... let go...

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Come on! Fight back! You've got those shackles. Use them!
No... I can't...

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tiny... if you don't take this seriously, you're going to die.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Take a guess. How many rivals do you think I tore apart with my own fangs to become the Mountain Lord?
Her growl swallows the alarms until they fade to distant buzzing. Your vision tunnels toward black. You are at the edge now. If you do not act—

Crimson light flares hot and sudden. Shackle marks bloom like burning brands where your skin meets hers. Perception and will snap together—yours and hers, one chain. Xiaofeng's body locks. Her fingertips still rest against your throat, but the pressure stops. She cannot push further.
Enough. I'm not here to fight you to the death. Or to prove who's stronger.
If you want a fight, maybe no one here can stop you. Not these people, not these walls, not this entire Bureau. But I'm not playing your game, the one that drags everyone into a dead end with you.
I'm not here to argue about who's right. I don't expect you to agree with me now. But I want to hear you out. And I hope... you'll hear me out too.
The pressure on your throat vanishes, and Xiaofeng takes half a step back. The excitement drains from her face, leaving only obvious disappointment.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...Forget it. I'm done. This is boring.
What...

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: I came looking for you because I thought maybe... Tch. I was wrong about you.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: You're no different from the rest of them. All those so-called heroes.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: ...Boring. I'm leaving.
You clutch your throat. The ghost of pressure still lingers around your windpipe. Xiaofeng shakes out her hands and rises to her feet.
Then the security team bursts in. Weapons snap up, every barrel trained on Xiaofeng. Grim faces, ready to fire. But you do not let them stop her. She walks out untouched.
...The ship back to Eastia is ready. It leaves in a few days.
You'll stay at the Bureau until then. If... whenever you feel like talking, I'll be here. You know where to find me.
Xiaofeng's ears twitch, but she says nothing and walks out of the interrogation room without looking back.
